audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill / Tryndamere / Tryndamere / Skill / Skill / Tryndamere / Tryndamere. The packet chart is Tryndamere / Tryndamere / Skill / Tryndamere / Sylas / Skill / Tryndamere.
audit.why: The content whys already argue the packet on five of the six disputed rows: whys[0] 'you have no engage tool — refuse extended trades', whys[3] 'every crit trade tilts toward him', whys[4] 'Hijack flips the lane', whys[5] 'your best extended-trade window', whys[6] 'avoid 1v1s'. Sylas 47.24% over 362 games is a losing lane and the packet's shape reflects that; the old chart handed Sylas the level-6 row as 'Skill' while its own why called it the flip.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3, 4, 5 moved to the packet chart as matched full+content pairs, with ratings on rows 0, 3 and 4 adjusted. No mirror audit exists for this matchup, so the packet plus the page's own prose is the evidence.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout does not appear anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Riot text: 'decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their BACKS TURNED to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.' 850 range, 14s. Two consequences the page never delivers: running away from him is what slows you, and the attack-damage half of it barely touches an AP Sylas.
audit.corrected: Walk toward him, never away. And do not spend E1's shield fearing Mocking Shout — save it for Spinning Slash.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page states that Bloodlust consumes Fury, or that Fury IS his crit chance.
audit.why: Battle Fury: 'Fury passively increases his Critical Strike Chance and can be consumed with his Bloodlust spell.' So the moment he casts Bloodlust to heal, his crit chance drops to nothing. That is the single cleanest trade window in the matchup and it is absent.
audit.corrected: Watch the Fury bar, not a cooldown: he heals, his crit collapses, you go.

audit.whatIsWrong: Slots are confused — whys[0] credits crits to a 'fury-passive' while spikes[0] calls it 'Tryndamere's Q passive fury stacks'. Fury is Battle Fury (P); Bloodlust (Q) is the heal.
audit.why: Bloodlust also raises his attack damage the more wounded he is, which is the reverse of how the page frames chip damage — poking him down makes him hit harder, not softer.
audit.corrected: Named each to its slot and stated the wounded-AD scaling in phases[3].why and whys[3].
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json (P and Q text, Q cd 12)

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d calls a wasted Undying Rage a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Undying Rage is 120/100/80. Fifteen is off by a factor of eight at rank 1. Against Hijack's 80/55/30 you actually hold a stolen copy on a shorter cooldown than his own, which is the real level-6 argument and the page never makes it.
audit.corrected: 120s at rank 1 against your 80s — roughly 40 seconds of every cycle where you have his panic button and he does not.

audit.why: whys[1] and the early paragraph claim 'his E gap-close has a shorter cooldown than your full E1-E2 sequence'. Checked and true: Spinning Slash is 12/11/10/9/8 against Abscond/Abduct's 13/12/11/10/9 — exactly one second shorter at every rank.
audit.corrected: Kept the claim and gave it the numbers in dontsFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appears once in report[8].t with no reason attached.
audit.why: Bloodlust is his entire sustain, on a flat 12s cooldown, and it converts Fury directly into health. Grievous Wounds does not just reduce healing here, it removes the reason he can stay in a losing lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad and dontsFull refer to losing 'no stun' with both E charges spent.
audit.why: Abscond/Abduct is a dash with a recast self-pull in Riot's text; no hardCC flag. Consistent with the calls made across this shard.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real risk — Spinning Slash off cooldown and no charges left.

notes: No mirror audit exists for this matchup, so whoever runs tryndamere should take three things from this file rather than re-deriving them: Undying Rage is 120/100/80 against Hijack's 80/55/30 (the page claimed a 'fifteen-second' window); Spinning Slash at 12/11/10/9/8 is exactly one second shorter than Abscond/Abduct at every rank, which the existing text asserted qualitatively and turns out to be right; and Mocking Shout only slows targets with their backs turned. That last one is the best addition — the ability was absent from the page entirely, and the counterplay (walk toward him, not away) is the opposite of instinct. Second-best: Fury IS his crit chance and Bloodlust consumes it, so his heal is also his crit dump and the cleanest trade window in the lane. Deliberately not written: the duration of Undying Rage. Every field said 'five seconds' but Riot's text gives no number, so I rewrote around it rather than repeat an unverified figure — recorded in unverified.
